metadata.query_context: Minimizing doxorubicin toxicity while preserving anti-tumor efficacy for NF1

cardioprotective_drugs.name: Dexrazoxane
cardioprotective_drugs.mechanism: Iron chelator that prevents doxorubicin-mediated free radical formation in cardiomyocytes; also acts as catalytic TOP2B inhibitor preventing anthracycline-TOP2B-mediated DNA damage in heart tissue
cardioprotective_drugs.approval_status: Approved for prevention of anthracycline-induced cardiotoxicity
cardioprotective_drugs.strategy: CARDIOPROTECTIVE - Reduces doxorubicin cardiotoxicity without compromising anti-tumor efficacy
cardioprotective_drugs.rationale: Only FDA-approved cardioprotectant for anthracycline therapy; prevents formation of cardiotoxic doxorubicinol metabolite and TOP2B-mediated DNA damage in cardiomyocytes
cardioprotective_drugs.clinical_evidence: Meta-analyses show 80% reduction in cardiac events without reducing tumor response rates

cardioprotective_drugs.name: All-trans retinoic acid (ATRA)
cardioprotective_drugs.mechanism: RARG nuclear receptor agonist that activates cardioprotective gene programs including antioxidant enzymes, anti-apoptotic factors, and mitochondrial biogenesis pathways
cardioprotective_drugs.approval_status: Approved for acute promyelocytic leukemia; investigational for cardioprotection
cardioprotective_drugs.strategy: CARDIOPROTECTIVE - RARG activation may prevent doxorubicin-induced cardiac dysfunction
cardioprotective_drugs.rationale: Phase 3 expansion identified RARG pathway as potential cardioprotective mechanism; retinoic acid signaling reduces oxidative stress and preserves mitochondrial function in cardiomyocytes
cardioprotective_drugs.clinical_evidence: Preclinical studies show RARG agonists reduce anthracycline cardiotoxicity; clinical trials ongoing

cardioprotective_drugs.name: Curcumin
cardioprotective_drugs.mechanism: Weak CBR1 inhibitor that reduces conversion of doxorubicin to cardiotoxic doxorubicinol metabolite; also provides antioxidant activity
cardioprotective_drugs.approval_status: Dietary supplement; investigational for anthracycline cardioprotection
cardioprotective_drugs.rationale: Phase 2 enrichment identified CBR1 as key enzyme converting doxorubicin to cardiotoxic doxorubicinol; CBR1 inhibition could reduce cardiac metabolite accumulation
cardioprotective_drugs.clinical_evidence: Phase 2 trials show modest cardioprotective effects; limited by poor bioavailability

efficacy_enhancing_drugs.name: Selumetinib
efficacy_enhancing_drugs.mechanism: Selective MEK1/2 inhibitor that blocks RAS-MAPK signaling hyperactivated in NF1-deficient tumors
efficacy_enhancing_drugs.approval_status: FDA approved 2020 for NF1-related plexiform neurofibromas in pediatric patients
efficacy_enhancing_drugs.strategy: EFFICACY-ENHANCING - Synergizes with doxorubicin in NF1-mutant tumors
efficacy_enhancing_drugs.rationale: NF1 loss causes hyperactive RAS-MAPK signaling; MEK inhibition is synthetically lethal with NF1 deficiency and may synergize with doxorubicin (TOP2A inhibition). Already approved for NF1 indication.
efficacy_enhancing_drugs.clinical_evidence: SPRINT trial: 66% response rate in NF1 plexiform neurofibromas; combination with anthracyclines under investigation

efficacy_enhancing_drugs.name: Sotorasib
efficacy_enhancing_drugs.mechanism: Covalent KRAS G12C inhibitor that locks KRAS in inactive GDP-bound state
efficacy_enhancing_drugs.approval_status: FDA approved 2021 for KRAS G12C-mutant non-small cell lung cancer
efficacy_enhancing_drugs.strategy: EFFICACY-ENHANCING - Targets KRAS synthetic lethality with NF1
efficacy_enhancing_drugs.rationale: Phase 3 expansion identified NF1-KRAS synthetic lethality (BioGRID PMID:19490893); KRAS inhibition may synergize with doxorubicin in NF1-mutant tumors. Mutation-specific (G12C).
efficacy_enhancing_drugs.clinical_evidence: 37% response rate in KRAS G12C NSCLC; combination trials with chemotherapy ongoing

efficacy_enhancing_drugs.name: Adagrasib
efficacy_enhancing_drugs.mechanism: Covalent KRAS G12C inhibitor with CNS penetration
efficacy_enhancing_drugs.approval_status: FDA approved 2022 for KRAS G12C-mutant non-small cell lung cancer
efficacy_enhancing_drugs.strategy: EFFICACY-ENHANCING - Targets KRAS synthetic lethality with NF1
efficacy_enhancing_drugs.rationale: Alternative KRAS G12C inhibitor with better CNS penetration; relevant for NF1-associated brain tumors (gliomas, optic pathway gliomas)
efficacy_enhancing_drugs.clinical_evidence: 42% response rate in KRAS G12C NSCLC; CNS activity demonstrated

efficacy_enhancing_drugs.name: Trametinib
efficacy_enhancing_drugs.mechanism: Selective allosteric MEK1/2 inhibitor blocking RAS-MAPK pathway
efficacy_enhancing_drugs.approval_status: FDA approved for BRAF-mutant melanoma; investigational for NF1
efficacy_enhancing_drugs.strategy: EFFICACY-ENHANCING - Blocks hyperactive MAPK signaling in NF1 loss
efficacy_enhancing_drugs.rationale: MEK sits downstream of both NF1 and KRAS in MAPK cascade; MEK inhibition addresses hyperactive signaling regardless of upstream mutation
efficacy_enhancing_drugs.clinical_evidence: Approved in combination with dabrafenib for melanoma; NF1 trials ongoing

efficacy_enhancing_drugs.name: Binimetinib
efficacy_enhancing_drugs.mechanism: Selective MEK1/2 inhibitor with improved CNS penetration
efficacy_enhancing_drugs.rationale: Better CNS penetration than other MEK inhibitors; relevant for NF1-associated CNS tumors (gliomas)
efficacy_enhancing_drugs.clinical_evidence: Approved for NRAS-mutant melanoma; CNS activity in preclinical models

efficacy_enhancing_drugs.name: Cetuximab
efficacy_enhancing_drugs.mechanism: Monoclonal antibody blocking EGFR ligand binding and receptor dimerization
efficacy_enhancing_drugs.approval_status: FDA approved for colorectal cancer and head/neck cancer
efficacy_enhancing_drugs.rationale: Phase 3 expansion identified NF1-EGFR positive genetic interaction (BioGRID PMID:31741433); EGFR inhibition blocks upstream RAS activation in NF1-deficient cells
efficacy_enhancing_drugs.clinical_evidence: Approved for KRAS wild-type colorectal cancer; combination with chemotherapy standard of care
efficacy_enhancing_drugs.provenance: Phase 3 BioGRID NF1-EGFR interaction, Clinical literature

selective_inhibitors.name: Mitoxantrone
selective_inhibitors.mechanism: Anthracenedione TOP2 inhibitor with ~10-fold selectivity for TOP2A over TOP2B
selective_inhibitors.approval_status: FDA approved for acute myeloid leukemia, prostate cancer, multiple sclerosis
selective_inhibitors.strategy: SELECTIVE - Preserves anti-tumor TOP2A inhibition with reduced TOP2B cardiotoxicity
selective_inhibitors.rationale: Phase 3 identified TOP2A-TOP2B heterodimerization as differential toxicity mechanism; mitoxantrone shows partial TOP2A selectivity reducing cardiotoxicity vs doxorubicin
selective_inhibitors.clinical_evidence: Lower cardiotoxicity than doxorubicin but still significant; not completely TOP2A-selective
selective_inhibitors.limitation: Only partial selectivity; still causes cardiotoxicity at high cumulative doses

selective_inhibitors.name: Etoposide
selective_inhibitors.mechanism: Podophyllotoxin derivative that stabilizes TOP2-DNA cleavage complex
selective_inhibitors.approval_status: FDA approved for testicular cancer, small cell lung cancer, lymphomas
selective_inhibitors.strategy: SELECTIVE - Alternative TOP2 poison with different toxicity profile
selective_inhibitors.rationale: Non-anthracycline TOP2 inhibitor with lower cardiotoxicity than doxorubicin; still hits both TOP2A and TOP2B but different tissue distribution
selective_inhibitors.clinical_evidence: Standard chemotherapy agent; cardiotoxicity much lower than anthracyclines
selective_inhibitors.limitation: Not truly selective; lower cardiotoxicity due to different pharmacokinetics

excluded_candidates.name: Direct CBR1 inhibitors
excluded_candidates.reason: No selective, clinically approved CBR1 inhibitors exist; curcumin has weak activity and poor bioavailability

excluded_candidates.name: Direct TOP2B inhibitors
excluded_candidates.reason: No selective TOP2B inhibitors available; all TOP2 poisons hit both isoforms. Selective TOP2B inhibition theoretically undesirable as it would block the mechanism of cardiotoxicity but we want to AVOID TOP2B inhibition, not enhance it.

excluded_candidates.name: Pan-RAS inhibitors
excluded_candidates.reason: Sotorasib and adagrasib are KRAS G12C-specific; pan-RAS inhibitors remain investigational with high toxicity

excluded_candidates.name: ABCB1 (P-gp) inhibitors
excluded_candidates.reason: While ABCB1 inhibitors could enhance doxorubicin tumor uptake, they also increase systemic toxicity and cardiotoxicity; unfavorable therapeutic window

excluded_candidates.name: RAF1 inhibitors
excluded_candidates.reason: No selective RAF1 inhibitors clinically available; RAF inhibitors paradoxically activate MAPK in KRAS-mutant contexts

filtering_rationale.nf1_context: NF1 is a loss-of-function tumor suppressor causing hyperactive RAS-MAPK signaling
filtering_rationale.therapeutic_strategy: Two-pronged approach: (1) CARDIOPROTECTIVE drugs reduce doxorubicin toxicity via TOP2B/CBR1/RARG modulation, (2) EFFICACY-ENHANCING drugs synergize with doxorubicin in NF1-deficient tumors via MAPK pathway inhibition
filtering_rationale.synthetic_lethality: NF1 loss creates dependencies on KRAS and TOP2A (Phase 3 BioGRID evidence); MEK/KRAS inhibitors exploit these vulnerabilities
filtering_rationale.mechanism_filter: Included inhibitors/antagonists of gain-of-function targets (KRAS, EGFR, MEK, TOP2B, CBR1); included agonists of protective targets (RARG)
filtering_rationale.clinical_maturity: Prioritized FDA-approved drugs (Phase 4) over investigational agents; selumetinib has specific NF1 approval

key_therapeutic_hypotheses.hypothesis: Selumetinib + doxorubicin combination for NF1-associated tumors
key_therapeutic_hypotheses.rationale: Selumetinib FDA-approved for NF1, addresses hyperactive MAPK signaling, may synergize with doxorubicin TOP2A inhibition
key_therapeutic_hypotheses.evidence_strength: HIGH - Phase 4 NF1 approval, Phase 3 BioGRID NF1-KRAS synthetic lethality
key_therapeutic_hypotheses.clinical_actionability: Highest priority - both drugs approved, NF1-specific

key_therapeutic_hypotheses.rationale: Only FDA-approved cardioprotectant for anthracyclines; prevents TOP2B-mediated cardiac DNA damage and doxorubicinol formation
key_therapeutic_hypotheses.evidence_strength: HIGH - Meta-analyses show 80% cardiac event reduction
key_therapeutic_hypotheses.clinical_actionability: Highest priority - standard of care for high-dose anthracyclines

key_therapeutic_hypotheses.hypothesis: KRAS G12C inhibitors (sotorasib/adagrasib) for G12C-mutant NF1 tumors
key_therapeutic_hypotheses.rationale: Subset of NF1-associated tumors may harbor concurrent KRAS G12C mutations; direct KRAS targeting addresses synthetic lethality
key_therapeutic_hypotheses.evidence_strength: MODERATE - Requires KRAS G12C mutation; not all NF1 tumors

key_therapeutic_hypotheses.rationale: Retinoic acid signaling activates cardioprotective gene programs; may prevent doxorubicin cardiac dysfunction
key_therapeutic_hypotheses.evidence_strength: LOW - Preclinical only, clinical trials ongoing

key_therapeutic_hypotheses.hypothesis: Mitoxantrone as TOP2A-preferential alternative to doxorubicin
key_therapeutic_hypotheses.rationale: Partial TOP2A selectivity may reduce cardiotoxicity while preserving anti-tumor efficacy in NF1-hypersensitive tumors
key_therapeutic_hypotheses.evidence_strength: MODERATE - Clinical use established, lower cardiotoxicity than doxorubicin
key_therapeutic_hypotheses.clinical_actionability: Medium - alternative anthracycline, not a combination

unresolved_targets.reason: No selective RAF1 inhibitors available; RAF inhibitors show paradoxical MAPK activation in RAS-mutant contexts
No selective CBR3 inhibitors; CBR1 and CBR3 have overlapping substrate specificity
TP53 is a tumor suppressor; restoration rather than inhibition desired; p53 reactivation compounds investigational
unresolved_targets.status: Conceptually important but no approved modulators for this context

unresolved_targets.reason: Tumor suppressors in DNA repair; PARP inhibitors exploit BRCA deficiency but NF1 tumors not typically BRCA-deficient
Nuclear receptors regulating drug metabolism; no direct therapeutic relevance for doxorubicin toxicity minimization

summary.data_limitations: ChEMBL API unavailable (timeouts); relied on PubChem and clinical literature. No direct CBR1 or TOP2B selective inhibitors exist in clinic.
